newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech leader doing well after cancer surgery.
newsitem.headline: Czech leader doing well after cancer surgery.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel, who had half of a lung with a malignant tumour removed earlier this week, is recuperating nicely with no signs of complications after the radical surgery, his spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The state of the patient is very good. The president has no (abnormal) temperature," Ladislav Spacek said in a statement.
He said laboratory samples "do not hint at any complications".
Czech surgeons decided to remove half Havel's right lung after finding a small malignant tumour during exploratory surgery on Monday.
Havel, a heavy smoker, was admitted to a Prague clinic on November 25 after his office claimed he had been suffering from pneumonia.
Doctors said the cancer had been caught in an early stage and the prognosis for Havel was positive.
Chief surgeon Pavel Pafko said on Monday that it was not possible to determine if the tumour resulted directly from Havel's smoking.
Havel, whose role as Czech president is more ceremonial than executive, could be back at home in about a week and might be back at work in about six weeks, Pafko said.
